**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/20 (Sat) 15:25
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The partial sums of the zeta function can be thought of as a random walk in the early stages and then resemble cornu spirals later on.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The real part of the zeta function is denoted by Re(ζ(s)).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The partial sum of the real part up to N terms is given by S(N) = 1 + 1/2^s + 1/3^s + ... + 1/N^s.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Using the Euler-Maclaurin formula, S(N) can be approximated as S(N) = ∫[1,N] Re(ζ(s)) ds + C(N), where C(N) is a correction term involving the Bernoulli numbers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] When N is small, there is only one sample per Nyquist mode and the partial sums look similar to a random walk.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The integral term can be approximated by a sum over the sample points: ∫[1,N] Re(ζ(s)) ds ≈ Σ[1,N] Re(ζ(k)).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Sample points are defined as s(k) = 2πik / ln(N+1), where k = 0, 1, 2, ..., N.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The centers of the cornu spirals correspond to the values of s(k) at which the phase of the summands changes by π/2.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The centers of the cornu spirals satisfy the equation: Im(s(k)) = π / (2 ln(N+1)).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The midpoint between each successive pair of sample points is defined as m(k) = (s(k) + s(k+1)) / 2.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Two sets of values are defined: R(k) = Re(ζ(s(k))) and M(k) = Re(ζ(m(k))).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] R(k) corresponds to the values used in the random walk approximation, while M(k) corresponds to the values at the centers of the cornu spirals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The midpoint values, M(k), are symmetric with respect to the random walk-like pattern, R(k).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The midpoint between the first two sample points is m(0) = (s(0) + s(1)) / 2 = π / ln(N+1), corresponding to
